heading: INT. OPERA HOUSE COAT CHECK ROOM - NIGHT

units.text: INT. OPERA HOUSE COAT CHECK ROOM - NIGHT
Racks of furs and top hats in the dim glow of a single bulb.
A velvet curtain divides the room from the lobby, where an aria swells, muffled.
SERAPHINA DUMONT (30s, ruby evening gown, a claim ticket pinched between gloved fingers) presses a hat check into the hand of the attendant, a skinny youth with oversized cufflinks.
Behind her, a tall figure in a doorman's coat keeps watch at the curtain: this is the STRANGER, handsome, impassive, a scar through one brow.
In the corner, an older woman in a fur stole examines the rack, LADY CORDELIA ASHBY-FORSYTHE (60s, diamonds heavy at her throat).
The attendant fetches a coat.
The stranger glances at Lady Cordelia, who has turned her back.
Seraphina slips a small silver key into the coat's lining while the attendant shakes out the sleeve, and the stranger, noticing her motion, slides smoothly between them and the curtain.
Madame, your coat.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Thank you.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: Is that the Dumont girl?
units.name: LADY CORDELIA

units.text: Lady Cordelia. How lovely.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: The attendant, flustered, drops a scarf.
Seraphina and the stranger both bend to catch it and their hands collide.
They look at each other, and in that look, a plan changes.
I do hope you're not leaving before the second act.
units.name: LADY CORDELIA

units.text: Never.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: The aria hits its high note.
As the room shakes, the stranger lifts the stole from Lady Cordelia's shoulders and, in the same breath, passes it to Seraphina, who drapes it over her arm like a waiter's towel.
My stole!
units.name: LADY CORDELIA

units.text: I believe it was mislaid, Madame.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Seraphina hands it back with an apologetic smile, but one diamond is gone from the hem.
The stranger's coat pocket rattles softly as he steps aside to let her pass.
Seraphina swans through the curtain.
The stranger, whom the attendant addresses as MR. DELACROIX-WEST, follows without a backward glance.
